messages:
maya: Hey folks — fresh hire here. Trying to run the app locally on my M1 Mac but it can't connect to Postgres in docker-compose. `docker-compose up` shows the db container as healthy but app logs keep spitting `could not connect to server: Connection refused`. Any quick checks?

sam: welcome! first things: can you paste your db service snippet from docker-compose.yml and the app's DB_HOST env? usually a port mapping or host name issue.

maya: here's the db section I'm using:
```
db:
  image: postgres:14
  volumes:
    - ./data/db:/var/lib/postgresql/data
  ports:
    - "5432:5432"
  environment:
    POSTGRES_PASSWORD: example
```
app ENV: `DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:example@localhost:5432/mydb`

oliver: ah — that DATABASE_URL points at localhost from your host's perspective. From the app container, `localhost` means the app container itself, not the db container. If your app is in a separate service in the same compose file, use the service name as host: `postgres://postgres:example@db:5432/mydb`.

lina: also on M1 a few people hit image arch mismatches. Try `docker-compose down -v` then add `platform: linux/amd64` under the db service if the image you pulled is amd64-only, or switch to an arm64-compatible tag.

sam: quick commands to debug: `docker-compose ps`, `docker-compose logs db`, and exec in the db: `docker-compose exec db pg_isready -U postgres` — that will tell you if Postgres is accepting connections.

maya: running `pg_isready` returned "/var/run/postgresql: No such file or directory". Logs show `could not change ownership of directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data": Operation not permitted`

oliver: volume mount permission problem — common when host directory UID/GID != postgres container UID (usually 999). Try `sudo chown -R 999:999 ./data/db` (or run without host mount to verify). If that fixes it, you can stick with the mount; otherwise use a named volume instead of a host path.

lina: for redis if you add it, remember service name resolution is the same. Use `redis://redis:6379/0` inside other services. And if any client tries to connect via a UNIX socket on mac it won't work cross-container. Use TCP host/port.

devex-bot: pinned: internal guide on M1 local dev with Postgres/Redis -> https://redwood.internal/dev/local-db-m1 (check section "volumes and platform").

maya: thanks — I changed DATABASE_URL to use `db` as host and chowned the folder. `docker-compose up` now shows Postgres ready and the app connects. Also removed the host bind and used a named volume per the guide.

sam: nice! glad it worked. If you want, drop your machine type in #new-hires so infra can add any extra tips for M1/M2 devs. :tada:

maya: will do, thanks everyone :)
